messages:
maya: FYI — after the token-smoothing and queue-policy tweak at 09:12 we started seeing a p95 latency increase on small chat completions and a throughput drop on the 4x GPU pool. p95 up ~25ms, throughput -12%. Anyone see traces?

raj: I pulled traces from the canary nodes. There's a clear change in batching behavior: lots more tiny batches forming and we hit kernel-selection fallback more often.

liam: Confirmed. Kernel router logs show spikes of 'fallback_kernel=generic_fp16' during the higher-latency windows. Sample log: `2026-03-17T09:13:02Z selected_kernel=vllm_fast seq_len=16 batch_size=1 fallback=0` then later `2026-03-17T09:13:02Z selected_kernel=generic_fp16 seq_len=16 batch_size=1 fallback=1`. Fallback rate jumped from 0.6% -> 4.8% on that pool.

sara: Also noticed KV cache hit rate on that pool dropped from ~94% to ~86% after the smoothing rollout. Hypothesis: token-smoothing injects short prefix tokens that prevent exact prefix cache matches, so prefix-based caching misses more often.

jess: Can we reproduce with load tests? I can run a small workload that mimics short-chat patterns. What exact config changed?

maya: Smoothing config was: `continuous_batching.token_smoothing.enabled=true; smoothing.window_ms=30; smoothing.min_prefix_tokens=2`. Queue policy changed to prefer latency SLOs (deprioritize long-waited small reqs) — that might be causing micro-batches.

raj: Ran local load: 10k short requests (avg 12 tokens) over 5 mins. Baseline p95=68ms, after smoothing p95=94ms. Kernel fallback correlates with requests that missed KV cache.

liam: Profiling CPU/GPU shows more frequent small memcpy/dispatch overhead when batch_size==1. The batching heuristic now sometimes flushes earlier when smoothing marks a partial window as steady. That interaction creates more single-request batches.

maya: Ops, starting a canary rollback of smoothing on one host to see if metrics revert.

ops-bot: deploy revert job started for service/runtime-canary-3 — job id 7c2f.

perf-bot: quick perf run on canary-3 before revert: p95=96ms, throughput=188 req/s. After revert (1 minute): p95=70ms, throughput=210 req/s. KV hit rate recovered to 93%.

sara: That looks like strong signal. Work items: (1) revert smoothing globally until we analyze; (2) investigate smoothing window/MS alignment with prefix cache granularity; (3) add guard to batching heuristic to avoid early flushes when estimated kernel fallback risk is high.

jess: +1. Also propose we add an experiment metric: 'prefix-normalized-kv-hit' that ignores trivial smoothing tokens so we can separate cache effect from true prefix mismatch.

raj: I'll open a short-lived feature-flagged patch to disable smoothing for requests under 24 tokens as a mitigation. If that stabilizes, we can iterate.

maya: Thanks. Can folks paste any interesting trace ids here if you see odd kernel routing patterns? I'll coordinate an incident page for the regression and schedule a follow-up postmortem if rollback is needed.

liam: trace ids I saw: trace-cc8a, trace-d4f1, trace-e02b — sent to perf dash.

maya: Great. For now rolling back smoothing on the rest of the canaries. I'll update when the global config is reversed. :thumbsup:
